Data source overview:
The provided “paper” is actually just the bibliography/reference list of some unknown manuscript, containing a long alphabetised list of citations without any accompanying abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion or conclusion.  It therefore contains no prose, no articulated risks/problems, no theoretical insights, no design rationales, no implementation mechanisms, no validation evidence and no proposed interventions.

Because every extraction step depends on detecting explicit (or at least inferable) causal reasoning linking risks → methods → findings → interventions, it is impossible to construct even a minimally connected knowledge fabric from a bare list of unrelated references.  Each citation points to a different external data source that might, independently, contain extractable reasoning chains, but within this document there is no connective text.

Result: No causal-interventional pathways can be extracted from this data source.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[10]
(Confidence is very low because the document simply lacks the information needed; the 10 reflects high confidence that no fabric can be extracted, not low confidence in the judgment.)

Inference-strategy justification:
Only minimal inference is permissible when some reasoning context is present.  Here no context exists.  Attempting to infer risks, problems or interventions purely from paper titles would amount to speculation well beyond the “moderate inference” allowance.  Consequently the only correct action is to declare extraction impossible.

Extraction completeness explanation:
All text was examined; no reasoning content exists.  Hence returning an empty fabric is complete and correct.

Key limitations:
1. A reference list alone is insufficient for knowledge-fabric extraction.
2. Without narrative context, titles alone cannot be reliably mapped into the six concept categories.

Possible prompt-improvement suggestion:
Detect reference-only sections automatically and skip extraction, or instruct the extractor to fetch the full papers instead.  Alternatively, permit harvesting of individual citation titles as seed nodes only if the downstream pipeline later merges them with full-text extractions.
